rule.sl:
Kar se je začelo nekoč in še traja, gre v present perfect: **I've lived here for ten years.** (Tu živim deset let.) **Jack has known Meg since she was a pup.** (Jack pozna Meg, odkar je bila mladiček.) Slovenščina reče sedanjik, angleščina have, has + deležnik. Na Irskem rečejo tudi *I'm here since Monday*; v pisanju je **I've been here since Monday**.

**for** + koliko časa: **for ten years**, **for a week**, **for ages**. **since** + kdaj se je začelo: **since 2016**, **since Monday**, **since I was a child** (v stavku za since past simple).

Vprašanje: **How long have you lived here?** (Odkdaj živiš tu?) Zanikano: **I haven't seen Jack for weeks.** **It hasn't rained since Monday.**

Kar je mimo, gre v past simple, tudi s for: **I lived in Leeds for five years.** (Zdaj ne več.) Z **ago** tudi: **I came here ten years ago.** ({m:Prišel|f:Prišla} sem pred desetimi leti.)
rule.de:
Was früher begonnen hat und noch andauert, steht im present perfect: **I've lived here for ten years.** (Ich wohne seit zehn Jahren hier.) **Jack has known Meg since she was a pup.** (Jack kennt Meg, seit sie ein Welpe war.) Deutsch sagt Präsens, Englisch have, has + Partizip. In Irland sagt man auch *I'm here since Monday*; geschrieben steht **I've been here since Monday**.

Deutsch hat für beides *seit*, Englisch zwei Wörter. **for** + wie lange: **for ten years**, **for a week**, **for ages**. **since** + wann es begann: **since 2016**, **since Monday**, **since I was a child** (im Satz nach since das past simple).

Frage: **How long have you lived here?** (Wie lange wohnst du schon hier?) Verneint: **I haven't seen Jack for weeks.** **It hasn't rained since Monday.**

Was vorbei ist, steht im past simple, auch mit for: **I lived in Leeds for five years.** (Jetzt nicht mehr.) Mit **ago** ebenso: **I came here ten years ago.** (Ich bin vor zehn Jahren gekommen.)
rule.it:
Ciò che è iniziato nel passato e dura ancora va al present perfect: **I've lived here for ten years.** (Vivo qui da dieci anni.) **Jack has known Meg since she was a pup.** (Jack conosce Meg da quando era una cucciola.) L'italiano usa il presente, l'inglese have, has + il participio. In Irlanda si dice anche *I'm here since Monday*; per iscritto **I've been here since Monday**.

L'italiano ha *da* per tutti e due, l'inglese due parole. **for** + quanto tempo: **for ten years**, **for a week**, **for ages**. **since** + quando è iniziato: **since 2016**, **since Monday**, **since I was a child** (nella frase dopo since il past simple).

Per chiedere: **How long have you lived here?** (Da quanto tempo vivi qui?) Negativo: **I haven't seen Jack for weeks.** **It hasn't rained since Monday.**

Ciò che è finito va al past simple, anche con for: **I lived in Leeds for five years.** (Adesso no.) Con **ago** lo stesso: **I came here ten years ago.** (Sono venut{m:o|f:a} dieci anni fa.)
rule.en:
What began in the past and still goes on takes the present perfect: **I've lived here for ten years.** **Jack has known Meg since she was a pup.** In Ireland people also say *I'm here since Monday*; writing wants **I've been here since Monday**.

**for** + how long: **for ten years**, **for a week**, **for ages**. **since** + when it began: **since 2016**, **since Monday**, **since I was a child** (the past simple in a clause after since).

To ask: **How long have you lived here?** To say no: **I haven't seen Jack for weeks.** **It hasn't rained since Monday.**

What is over takes the past simple, with for too: **I lived in Leeds for five years.** (I don't now.) With **ago** too: **I came here ten years ago.**

tip.sl: 💡 Slovenščina reče sedanjik (*tu živim deset let*), angleščina **I've lived**. Za *od* je **since**, za dolžino **for**.
tip.de: 💡 Deutsch sagt *seit* und Präsens (*seit zehn Jahren wohne ich*), Englisch **I've lived** und zwei Wörter: Dauer **for**, Beginn **since**.
tip.it: 💡 L'italiano dice *da* e il presente (*vivo qui da dieci anni*), l'inglese **I've lived** e due parole: durata **for**, inizio **since**.
tip.en: 💡 A length: **for**. A starting point: **since**. Either way **have**, **has** + the participle.
